question: In an examination, 50% of candidates failed in Mathematics and 75% failed in English. If 15% failed in both subjects, find the percentage of candidates who passed in both subjects.
explanation: Let the total population be 100%. We need to find the percentage belonging to at least one category. | Percentage belonging to at least one = 100% - Percentage belonging to neither. | $$100 - 15 = 85\%$$ | Using the set theory formula for intersections: | $$Both = n(the first subject) + n(the second subject) - n(\text{At least one})$$ | Substituting the given values: | $$Both = 50 + 75 - 85 = 40\%$$ | The final percentage of the population that belongs to both the first subject and the second subject is 40%.
